input.text: Root follow-up on the new I/O ordering in WriteBoundary.write: its previous final github.metadata check now occurs BEFORE the second admit_predecessors call, which performs multiple remote downloads/metadata requests. Test revoking the CONSUMER approval/run during that second predecessor acquisition while its credential/preview remains unexpired. The new expensive dependency work must not bypass the existing final consumer revocation check. Keep a final consumer metadata recheck after the new remote work and final local freshness/expiry/binding checks immediately before submit (avoid introducing infinite revalidation). Add actual regression evidence and retain previous authorization invariants. This is about preserving T003 behavior when adding I/O, not asserting impossible atomic cloud/GitHub revocation semantics.
